defs.def: a strong feeling of surprise as a result of sth happening, especially sth unpleasant; the event that causes this feeling 震惊；惊愕；令人震惊的事

ex.s: In her first PE class , Eva was shocked when Coach Pitt announced that everyone had to run one mile around the track outside.
ex.t: 在第一节体育课上，伊娃震惊地发现皮特教练宣布每个人都必须绕着外面的跑道跑一英里。

ex.s: So I was shocked when, not long after the email, Professor Mary Devon, who was running the programme, invited me to observe the work being done in her lab.
ex.t: 所以，在那封邮件之后不久，负责该项目的玛丽·德文教授邀请我去观察她的实验室工作时，我感到非常震惊。

ex.s: I jumped at the chance, and a few weeks later I was equally shocked—and overjoyed—when she invited me to talk with her about potential projects I could pursue in her lab.
ex.t: 我毫不犹豫地抓住了这个机会，几周后，当她邀请我与她讨论我可以在她的实验室里开展的潜在项目时，我同样震惊——而且欣喜若狂。

ex.s: “People from cultures that value relationships more than ours does are shocked by the thought of eating alone in front of a computer”, says Art Markman, a professor of psychology at the University of Texas, Austin.
ex.t: "来自比我们更重视人际关系的文化背景的人会对在电脑前独自吃饭的想法感到震惊，"德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校心理学教授Art Markman说。

ex.s: His reply came as a surprise — a shock, actually: “Not a chance.” Clearly, he was unhappy over the way we had parted.
ex.t: 他的回复令人意外——其实是震惊：“绝不可能。”显然，他对我们分开时的方式感到不快。

ex.s: He was even shocked at their wedding when he saw how the Chinese ate almost every part of an animal.
ex.t: 他甚至对他们的婚礼感到震惊，因为他看到中国人几乎吃掉了动物的每一个部分。

ex.s: Shortly before her sixteen birthday, she is shocked by the life-changing news that she is the princess of a fictional kingdom called Genovia.
ex.t: 在她十六岁生日前不久，她被一个改变人生的消息震惊了：她是一个叫做吉诺维亚的虚构王国的公主。

ex.s: Anne was shocked by the decision and did not know what to do.
ex.t: Anne对这个决定感到震惊，不知道该怎么办。

ex.s: A shocked Winton watched as the majority of people rose to their feet.
ex.t: 震惊的温顿看着大多数人站了起来。

ex.s: When I recovered from the shock, I looked at my camera.
ex.t: 当我从惊吓中回过神来，我看了看相机。

defs.def: a serious medical condition, usually the result of injury in which a person has lost a lot of blood and they are extremely weak 休克
a violent shaking movement that is caused by an explosion, earthquake, etc. （由爆炸、地震等引起的）剧烈震动，剧烈震荡

ex.s: The shock of it is like pressing a switch.
ex.t: 那种冲击就像按下一个开关。

defs.def: 别碰那根电线，不然会触电的。
a thick mass of hair on a person's head 浓密的一堆（头发）
to surprise and upset sb 使震惊；使惊愕

ex.s: Shocked for her own lack of hand skills.
ex.t: 对自己缺乏动手能力感到震惊。

defs.def: to make sb feel offended or disgusted 脏话、不道德行为等
